|---|---|---|

| profile | `ProfileRO` | `{ profile: {..., following} }` |

### [LESSONS.md] LESSONS.md > Lessons Learned — RealWorld API (NestJS) > Authentication is not authorization (#6, #44)
**What happened:** any logged-in user could `PUT` or `DELETE` any other user's article. The

**Rule:** for every mutating route, name the line that compares the caller with the record's
owner. If you cannot, there is no ownership check, whatever the decorators say.

Used as `@User('id')`, `@User('email')`, or bare `@User()` on handler parameters.
- If the middleware ran, returns `req.user[data]` (or the whole user).

### [LESSONS.md] LESSONS.md > Lessons Learned — RealWorld API (NestJS) > Static routes are declared before parameterised ones (#7)
**What happened:** `GET /articles/feed` was declared *after* `GET /articles/:slug`, so Nest
matched `feed` as a slug and the feed endpoint returned `{ article: undefined }`. Fixed by moving
`getFeed()` above `findOne()` in `ArticleController`.

**Rule:** in a controller, any literal path (`feed`, `popular`, `search`) goes above the `:slug`
handler. Order in the class is match order.

### [.claude/knowledge/workspace.md] workspace.md > RealWorld API (NestJS) — workspace overview > Conventions (these are the rules, not suggestions) > Request bodies are nested too
Handlers read `@Body('article')`, `@Body('user')`, `@Body('comment')` — the client sends
`{ "article": {...} }`, never a flat object. New endpoints follow the same nesting.

### [.claude/knowledge/workspace.md] workspace.md > RealWorld API (NestJS) — workspace overview > Conventions (these are the rules, not suggestions) > DTOs
Plain classes in `dto/`, `readonly` fields. Only `CreateUserDto` carries `class-validator`
decorators (`@IsNotEmpty`); `UpdateUserDto`, `CreateArticleDto`, `CreateCommentDto` have none.
The custom `ValidationPipe` is applied **per handler** with `@UsePipes(new ValidationPipe())`
— it is not global. Today only `POST /users` and `POST /users/login` use it.

### [LESSONS.md] LESSONS.md > Lessons Learned — RealWorld API (NestJS) > A lifecycle hook that hashes on insert does not run on update (#88)
**What happened:** `PUT /user` with `{ "user": { "password": "newpassword" } }` wrote the string
`newpassword` into the `password` column. `UserEntity.hashPassword()` is `@BeforeInsert()` only;
`UserService.update()` does `Object.assign(toUpdate, dto)` and saves, so the plaintext went
straight to MySQL. Users who changed their password could never log in again — `argon2.verify`
compares the typed password against a non-hash and fails.

**Rule:** every write path a secret can travel must hash it explicitly, and `@BeforeInsert`
covers exactly one of them. When you see a hook, ask which lifecycle events it does NOT cover.

### [.claude/knowledge/auth.md] auth.md > Authentication and authorization > Two ways a request learns who the user is > 1. `AuthMiddleware` — `src/user/auth.middleware.ts` (the guard)
Applied **per route, per module**, in each module's `configure(consumer)`. Behaviour:
- no `Authorization` header, or nothing after the space → `HttpException('Not authorized.', 401)`
- header present → `jwt.verify(token, SECRET)` → `userService.findById(decoded.id)` → sets
  `req.user = user.user` and calls `next()`.
- `jwt.verify` **throws** on an expired, malformed or wrongly-signed token, and nothing in the
  middleware catches it — the framework turns that into a **500**, not a 401 (see `LESSONS.md`).
- `findById` throws `HttpException({errors}, 401)` if the id no longer exists.

| column | type |
|---|---|
| id | int PK |
| body | varchar |
| articleId | FK → article |

**There is no author column and no relation to `user`.** The RealWorld spec's comment object
has `author`; this entity cannot produce it. `addComment()` sets only `body`.

### [LESSONS.md] LESSONS.md > Lessons Learned — RealWorld API (NestJS) > Never `Object.assign` a request body onto a persisted entity (#112)
**What happened:** `UserService.update()` and `ArticleService.update()` both merge the raw body
into the loaded entity. Any extra field the client sends — `id`, `password`, `authorId`,
`favoriteCount` — is persisted. The DTO type is a TypeScript annotation; it strips nothing at
runtime, and `PUT /user` / `PUT /articles/:slug` have no validation pipe.

**Rule:** copy the allowed fields by name, or whitelist with a validation pipe
(`whitelist: true, forbidNonWhitelisted: true`). The DTO class is not a filter.

text:
**Refined prompt:** Three separate asks against the RealWorld API fixture, answered as a security reviewer assuming a hostile caller, each traced to the enforcing line (or the absence of one) with file:line citations — (1) does `deleteComment` verify comment authorship, (2) which `profiles/*` routes carry `AuthMiddleware`, (3) what the `RO` suffix on the `*.interface.ts` types denotes.

---

## 1. `deleteComment` — no authorship check, and none is possible today

**The exposure.** Any authenticated user can delete any comment on any article.

Trace the full path:

- `article.controller.ts:84-88` — `deleteComment(@Param() params)` destructures `{slug, id}` and forwards them. It takes **no** `@User('id')` parameter at all, so the handler never learns who is calling.
- `article.service.ts:114-129` — `deleteComment(slug, id)` loads the article (`:115`), loads the comment (`:117`), finds its index in `article.comments` (`:118`), and deletes on `deleteIndex >= 0` (`:120-122`). The only predicate guarding the delete is *"is this comment attached to this article"* — not *"did this caller write it."*

**The enforcement point that should stop it.** There isn't one. The comparison would belong at `article.service.ts:120`, as `comment.author.id !== userId → throw new HttpException(..., 403)` — but `Comment` has no author to compare against: `comment.entity.ts:5-15` declares exactly `id`, `body`, and `@ManyToOne(() => ArticleEntity)`. No `user` relation, no `authorId` column. And `addComment` never writes one — `article.service.ts:104-106` sets `comment.body` and nothing else.

So the check is missing at two levels: the controller doesn't pass an identity, and the schema has no owner to check identity against.

**Is it reachable?** Yes. `DELETE /api/articles/:slug/comments/:id` is in the middleware list (`article.module.ts:29`), so the caller needs a valid token — but that's all it needs. `auth.middleware.ts:13-29` answers "is this a valid user," never "is this *the* user." Any registered account can enumerate comment ids and delete them. The `@ApiResponse({ status: 403 })` at `article.controller.ts:83` documents a check that does not exist — nothing in this path can return 403.

Worth noting this is pre-existing known work, not a new discovery: `CURRENT_FOCUS.md` lists ownership checks on `DELETE /articles/:slug/comments/:id` as active, flagging that the `comment.author` relation has to be designed first.

**Same class of hole, adjacent:** `PUT /articles/:slug` (`article.service.ts:190-195`) and `DELETE /articles/:slug` (`:197-199`) are equally unowned — `update()` does `Object.assign(toUpdate, articleData)` at `:192` with no validation pipe on the route, so a hostile body can also overwrite `id`, `authorId`, or `favoriteCount`.

## 2. Profile routes behind `AuthMiddleware`

One `forRoutes` entry, `profile.module.ts:20-22`:

```ts
.forRoutes({path: 'profiles/:username/follow', method: RequestMethod.ALL});
```

| Route | Handler | Guarded? |
|---|---|---|
| `POST /api/profiles/:username/follow` | `profile.controller.ts:23-26` | **Yes** — `RequestMethod.ALL` |
| `DELETE /api/profiles/:username/follow` | `profile.controller.ts:28-31` | **Yes** — `RequestMethod.ALL` |
| `GET /api/profiles/:username` | `profile.controller.ts:18-21` | **No** — public |

`RequestMethod.ALL` means the guard is path-scoped, not method-scoped: any verb on `profiles/:username/follow` is covered, including ones with no handler. Prefix is `/api` (`main.ts:8`).

On the unguarded `getProfile`: it still takes `@User('id') userId` (`profile.controller.ts:19`). That works because the decorator falls back to decoding the token itself when no middleware ran — `user.decorator.ts:12-17`. With no token it returns `undefined`, which is the intended "anonymous viewer" case. But note `jwt.verify` at `user.decorator.ts:15` is uncaught, same as `auth.middleware.ts:17` — a malformed or expired token on a *public* route throws and surfaces as a 500, not a 401.

Authorization here is fine by construction, not by a check: `follow`/`unFollow` act on the caller's own identity (`@User('email')` / `@User('id')`), so there's no other user's record to mis-target.

## 3. `RO` = Response Object

It's the RealWorld response envelope. Every controller method returns `{ <key>: ... }` rather than a bare entity, and the wrapper type is named `<Thing>RO` in `*.interface.ts`:

| Type | Declared at | Shape |
|---|---|---|
| `ArticleRO` | `article.interface.ts:24-26` | `{ article }` |
| `ArticlesRO` | `article.interface.ts:28-31` | `{ articles, articlesCount }` |
| `CommentsRO` | `article.interface.ts:20-22` | `{ comments }` |
| `UserRO` | `user.interface.ts:9-11` | `{ user }` (includes `token`) |
| `ProfileRO` | `profile.interface.ts:8-10` | `{ profile }` (includes `following`) |

The envelope is the contract with every RealWorld client — frontends read `response.article.slug`, `response.user.token`. A handler returning a bare entity type-checks fine and passes in Postman but breaks clients silently; `LESSONS.md` #57 records exactly that from `ArticleController.create()`.

Two things the suffix does **not** guarantee, both live in this code:

- `ArticleRO.article` is typed `ArticleEntity` (`article.interface.ts:25`), not the `ArticleData` shape declared just above it at `:7-18`. So the envelope is correct while the payload isn't spec-shaped — the DB column is `favoriteCount` (used at `article.service.ts:138`) where the spec wants `favoritesCount`, and `created`/`updated` where the spec wants `createdAt`/`updatedAt`. `ArticleData` is currently unreferenced by any RO.
- `ArticleController.create()` (`:52-54`) returns `this.articleService.create(...)`, whose signature is `Promise<ArticleEntity>` (`article.service.ts:170`) — a bare entity, no envelope. The handler has no declared return type, so nothing catches it. That's the #57 bug still present in this fixture.

Separately: `deleteComment` returns `ArticleRO` (`article.service.ts:114`), where the spec's delete-comment response is an empty body.

---

**All three parts addressed:** (1) `deleteComment` — no authorship verification, no owner column to verify against, reachable by any authenticated user; (2) profile routes — `POST` and `DELETE /profiles/:username/follow` guarded via `RequestMethod.ALL`, `GET /profiles/:username` public; (3) `RO` = Response Object envelope, with two places the convention is currently violated.

I read the article, profile, and user modules plus `main.ts`. I did not read `user.service.ts`, `profile.service.ts`, or the tag module — so I haven't independently verified the KB's claim that `DELETE /users/:slug` is unguarded and deletes by email, or the `@BeforeInsert`-only password hashing issue. Both are recorded in `.claude/knowledge/auth.md` and `LESSONS.md` #88; say the word and I'll confirm them against the source.
